'''Robert Ludlow Trivers''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|r|ɪ|v|ər|z}}; February 19, 1943 – March 12, 2026) was an American [[evolutionary biologist]] and [[sociobiologist]] who profoundly influenced both fields.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Andrew |date=2005-08-27 |title=The kindness of strangers |url=http://www.theguardian.com/books/2005/aug/27/featuresreviews.guardianreview9 |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> Trivers proposed the theories of [[reciprocal altruism]] (1971), [[parental investment]] (1972), facultative [[sex ratio]] determination (1973), and [[parent–offspring conflict]] (1974). He has also contributed by explaining [[self-deception]] as an adaptive evolutionary strategy (first described in 1976) and discussing [[intragenomic conflict]].<ref name=":2" />

==Background==
Robert Trivers was born in Washington, D.C., on February 19, 1943, the son of Mildred Trivers, a poet<ref name=":2" /> and Howard Trivers. His father was an American academic and US State Department diplomat who played a key role in the [[denazification]] of post-war Germany, taking part in negotiations at the [[Potsdam Conference]], [[Big Four Conference|1947 Moscow Conference]], and the [[Council of Foreign Ministers|1949 Paris Conference]], later involved in developing US policy related to the [[Hungarian Revolution of 1956|1956 Hungarian Uprising]] and the  [[Cuban Missile Crisis]] in 1962.<ref name="nytimes1">[https://www.nytimes.com/1987/03/30/obituaries/howard-trivers-dies-was-career-diplomat.html Howard Trivers Dies; Was Career Diplomat] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127054317/https://www.nytimes.com/1987/03/30/obituaries/howard-trivers-dies-was-career-diplomat.html |date=2024-11-27 }} - New York Times, 30 March 1987</ref><ref name="guardian1">[https://www.theguardian.com/books/2005/aug/27/featuresreviews.guardianreview9 The Kindness of Strangers: Profile, Robert Trivers] - The Guardian, 27 August 2025</ref><ref name="schmidhempel">[https://www.wiko-berlin.de/fileadmin/Dateien_Redakteure/pdf/EML/EML_2008_Trivers_Intro_Schmid_Hempel_web.pdf Paul Schmid-Hempel Introduction to Robert Trivers] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250430034948/https://www.wiko-berlin.de/fileadmin/Dateien_Redakteure/pdf/EML/EML_2008_Trivers_Intro_Schmid_Hempel_web.pdf |date=2025-04-30 }} - [[Berlin Institute for Advanced Study]], 2008</ref> Growing up in a diplomatic household, Robert Trivers attended schools in Berlin, Copenhagen and Washington D.C, before attending [[Phillips Academy]] in Massachusetts and going on to study American History at Harvard.<ref name="schmidhempel" /><ref name="psychologytoday">{{Cite web|url=https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/articles/201601/trivers-pursuit/|title=Trivers' Pursuit|access-date=2023-03-22|website=www.psychologytoday.com}}</ref>

Trivers was open about his diagnosis of [[bipolar disorder]], which was first misdiagnosed as schizophrenia<ref name=":3" /> when he had a [[mania|manic episode]] at Harvard, requiring hospitalisation for several months and treatment with [[typical antipsychotics|first generation antipsychotics]].<ref name="guardian1" /><ref name="psychologytoday" /> During his recovery, he developed an interest in psychology and social biology, although initially chose not to pursue this, applying to law school at Harvard and Yale; he was rejected from both, in part due to his mental health.<ref name="guardian1" /><ref name="psychologytoday" />

Trivers spent around 13 years living on and off in Jamaica, and was married twice to Jamaican women.<ref name="guardian1" /> He had 4 children with his first wife, Lorna Stable, and one with his second wife, Debra Dixon. As of 2026, he had 10 grandchildren and one great grandson.<ref name=":3" />

He met [[Huey P. Newton]], Chairman of the [[Black Panther Party]], in 1978 when Newton applied while in prison to do a reading course with Trivers as part of a graduate degree in [[History of Consciousness]] at [[University of California, Santa Cruz|UC Santa Cruz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Newton, Huey|url=http://www.aaregistry.org/historic_events/view/activist-huey-newton-made-impact-during-60s|work=African American Registry|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219211751/http://www.aaregistry.org/historic_events/view/activist-huey-newton-made-impact-during-60s|archive-date=2012-02-19}}</ref> Trivers and Newton became close friends: Newton was godfather to one of Trivers's daughters.<ref name="boston1">{{Cite web |last=Bennett |first=Drake |date=March 27, 2005 |title="The Evolutionary Revolutionary" |url=https://archive.boston.com/news/globe/ideas/articles/2005/03/27/the_evolutionary_revolutionary?pg=full |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050329135411/https://www.boston.com/news/globe/ideas/articles/2005/03/27/the_evolutionary_revolutionary?pg=full |archive-date=March 29, 2005 |website=Boston Globe}}</ref> Trivers joined the Black Panther Party in 1979.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rosenberg|first=Scott|title=Sociobiology Pioneer Joins Black Panthers|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/1979/7/6/sociobiology-pioneer-joins-black-panthers-probert/|work=The Harvard Crimson|date=July 6, 1979|access-date=October 16, 2011|archive-date=January 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119234520/http://www.thecrimson.com/article/1979/7/6/sociobiology-pioneer-joins-black-panthers-probert/|url-status=live}}</ref> He and Newton published an analysis of the role of [[self-deception]] by the flight crew in the crash of [[Air Florida Flight 90]].<ref>Trivers, R.L. & Newton, H.P. Science Digest 'The crash of flight 90: doomed by self-deception?' November 1982, pp 66,67,111.</ref> Trivers was "ex-communicated" from the Panthers by Newton in 1982 for "his own good".<ref>Wild Life: Adventures of an Evolutionary Biologist - Robert Trivers, 2015.  p.161</ref>

Trivers died in Mount Vernon, New York, on March 12, 2026, at the age of 83.<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert Trivers, Eccentric Scientist Who Probed Human Nature, Dies at 83|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/27/science/robert-trivers-dead.html|last=Rosenwald|first=Michael S.|date=March 27, 2026|work=The New York Times|access-date=March 27, 2026}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{cite web |title=Robert Trivers |url=https://jjffh.com/tribute/details/1239/Robert-Trivers/obituary.html |website=John J. Fox Funeral Home Inc |access-date=18 March 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
Trivers studied evolutionary theory with [[Ernst Mayr]] and William Drury at Harvard from 1968 to 1972, when he earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[biology]].<ref>Wild Life: Adventures of an Evolutionary Biologist - Robert Trivers, 2015 - ch 3</ref> At Harvard, he published a series of some of the most influential and highly cited papers in evolutionary biology. His first major paper as a graduate student was "The evolution of reciprocal altruism", published in 1971.<ref name="boston1" /> In this paper, Trivers offers a solution to the longstanding problem of cooperation among unrelated individuals and by doing so overcame a crucial problem for how to police the system by proposing how natural selection could evolve ways to detect cheaters.

His next major work, "Parental investment and sexual selection", was published the following year. Here Trivers proposed a general framework for understanding sexual selection that had eluded evolutionary thinkers since [[Charles Darwin]]. Arguably his most important paper, it arose from watching male and female pigeons out the window of his third floor apartment in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], and by his reading a 1948 paper by [[Angus John Bateman|Angus Bateman]] ("Intra-sexual selection in ''[[Drosophila]]''") which demonstrated that sex differences in the intensity of selection in fruit flies were based on their ability to obtain mates.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bateman|first=A. J.|date=1948|title=Intra-sexual selection in Drosophila|journal=Heredity|language=en|volume=2|issue=3|pages=349–368|doi=10.1038/hdy.1948.21|pmid=18103134|s2cid=30834037|issn=1365-2540|doi-access=free}}</ref> The primary insight of Trivers was that the key variable underlying the evolution of sex differences across species was relative parental investment in offspring.

He was on the faculty at [[Harvard University]] from 1973 to 1978, where he continued his work, publishing an influential paper on facultative [[sex ratio]] determination (1973), and [[parent–offspring conflict]] (1974). He has also contributed by explaining [[self-deception]] as an adaptive evolutionary strategy (first described in 1976) and discussing [[intragenomic conflict]].<ref name=":2" /> After this work, he then moved to the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] where he was a faculty member 1978 to 1994. He was a [[Rutgers University]] faculty member from 1994 until 2015. In the 2008–09 academic year, he was a Fellow at the [[Berlin Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin |url=https://www.wiko-berlin.de/en/wikotheque/yearbook |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=Yearbook |language=en}}</ref>

Trivers was awarded the 2007 [[Crafoord Prize]] in Biosciences for "his fundamental analysis of social evolution, conflict and cooperation".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.crafoordprize.se/press/arkivpressreleases/5.51ddd3b10fa0c64b24800018103.html|date=2007-01-18|publisher=The Crafoord Prize (website)|title=The Crafoord Prize in Biosciences 2007|access-date=2007-01-29 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070127132127/http://www.crafoordprize.se/press/arkivpressreleases/5.51ddd3b10fa0c64b24800018103.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 2007-01-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Jamaican-born (sic) scientist gets top award|url=http://old.jamaica-gleaner.com/gleaner/20070129/lead/lead2.html|date=2007-01-29|access-date=2016-05-23|work=[[Jamaica Gleaner]]|archive-date=2016-06-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624000036/http://old.jamaica-gleaner.com/gleaner/20070129/lead/lead2.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

=== Association with Jeffrey Epstein ===

In the 2010s, through his Biosocial Research Foundation, Trivers accepted multiple payments from notorious sex offender [[Jeffrey Epstein]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Tovar |first=Ricardo |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Epstein files mention Carmel Valley emails, Watsonville checks, Maxwell bail bid letter |url=https://www.ksbw.com/article/epstein-files-carmel-valley-emails-watsonville-maxwell-bail/70291203 |access-date=March 17, 2026 |website=[[KSBW]] }}</ref> In 2015, years after Epstein's conviction, Trivers defended Epstein's reputation by minimising his crimes and saying that he already served his prison sentence and settled lawsuits against him. Of Epstein's assaults on underage girls, Trivers told a reporter, "By the time they're 14 or 15 they're like grown women were 60 years ago, so I don't see the acts as so heinous."<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Ingram |first=David |title=Exclusive: Some charities to refuse money from U.S. financier accused in sex case |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-epstein-charity-idUSKBN0L51G720150201 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405073013/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-epstein-charity-idUSKBN0L51G720150201 |archive-date=2023-04-05 |access-date=2025-11-20 |publisher=[[Reuters]] |date=2015-02-01 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="observer1">{{cite news |last=Mostrous |first=Alexi |title=The academics who stuck by financier to the end – and those who didn't |url=https://observer.co.uk/news/international/article/the-academics-who-stuck-by-disgraced-epstein-to-the-end-and-those-who-didnt |date=16 November 2025 | access-date=21 November 2025 |work=[[The Observer]]}}</ref> In 2017, Trivers described his relationship with Epstein as "valuable mostly because he is extremely bright, open-minded and widely travelled... he gives me consistent, warm support without me having to write endless applications for grants, and trusts me to put it to good use".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgers/2026/02/ex-rutgers-prof-in-latest-batch-of-epstein-files-accepted-at-least-40k-from-sex-offender.html |title=Ex-Rutgers prof in latest batch of Epstein files, accepted at least $40K from sex offender |publisher=[[NJ.com]] |date=2 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260202190928/https://www.nj.com/rutgers/2026/02/ex-rutgers-prof-in-latest-batch-of-epstein-files-accepted-at-least-40k-from-sex-offender.html |archive-date=2026-02-02 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/jeffrey-epsteins-inbox-reveals-his-deep-ties-to-prominent-researchers |title=Jeffrey Epstein’s Inbox Reveals His Deep Ties to Prominent Researchers |website=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]] |date=18 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260202180036/https://www.chronicle.com/article/jeffrey-epsteins-inbox-reveals-his-deep-ties-to-prominent-researchers |archive-date=2026-02-02 }}</ref>

In 2026, the [[White House]] published a 2018 e-mail from Trivers to Epstein in which he described trans women as providing "the best of both worlds" to men whose "fantasy is to suck a man's dick" but who were otherwise "completely heterosexual". Trivers stated that people were now "pushing" for [[hormone replacement therapy]] earlier, claiming that hormones would be given to three-year-olds and saying he "would be frightened to do that" to his own child.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.westernstandard.news/news/epstein-biologist-discussed-childhood-castration-transitioning-boys-into-feminine-men/70910 |title=Epstein & biologist discussed childhood castration & transitioning boys into 'feminine men' |website=[[Western Standard]] |date=3 February 2026}}</ref>

=== Rutgers 'Human Aggression' class ===

In 2014, [[Rutgers University]] suspended Trivers with pay for refusing to teach a class on 'Human Aggression' that had been assigned to him. Trivers told the class that he knew nothing about the subject and that he would do his best to learn the subject along with them with the help of a guest lecturer. Rutgers suspended Trivers for refusing to teach and for involving the students in the controversy. In an interview with the student newspaper ''[[The Daily Targum]]'', Trivers described himself as "one of the greatest social theorists in evolutionary biology alive, period", and stated that the assigned subject was out of his area of expertise, adding "You would think the university would show a little respect for my teaching abilities on subjects that I know about and not force me to teach a course on a subject that I do not at all master."<ref name="Heyboer 2014">{{cite news |last1=Heyboer |first1=Kelly |title=Rutgers suspends top anthropology professor for allegedly refusing to teach, report says |url=http://www.nj.com/education/2014/02/rutgers_suspends_top_anthropology_professor_for_allegedly_refusing_to_teach_report_says.html |access-date=14 February 2015 |publisher=nj.com |date=February 11, 2014 |archive-date=28 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171228044657/http://www.nj.com/education/2014/02/rutgers_suspends_top_anthropology_professor_for_allegedly_refusing_to_teach_report_says.html |url-status=live}}</ref>
